terra.problem: The text says the father welcomed the Levite, but not that he greeted him at the door.
Saying he was not going to drag her home adds a detail about his intentions that the text does not give.
The text says he got up early, not that he planned to leave at sunrise.
The passage does not describe four days of requests for one more night. The father persuades him to remain three days, then makes further requests on the fourth and fifth days.
The comment about the Levite not having that much patience assigns him a trait the text does not give, without marking it as a guess.
Judges 19:10 identifies Jebus as Jerusalem, but does not say Jebus is its old name.
The cookie-sheet-cooling comparison does not clearly match the servant's suggestion to stop for the night.
The text says the sun set as they neared Gibeah, before the Levite sat in the square. It also does not say he chose Gibeah because Israelites lived there.
The passage does not say the old man was the first person in Gibeah to speak with the Levite.
The old man asks where the traveler is going and where he came from. Saying he wants to know who the traveler is adds an unstated intention.
The Levite also names Bethlehem in Judah when describing his trip, so the hill country and the house of the LORD are not the only two places he names.
The explanation refers to the next card, exposing the lesson structure.
What happens next is described in the same verse, Judges 19:25, not the following verse.
Exodus 12:41 does not say Egypt is where the Israelites started out as a nation.
The claim about when Babylon comes into Israel's history is outside the passage and has no reference. The explanation also states that the people were shocked without marking that feeling as a guess.
The people's stated starting point is the departure from Egypt, not all of Israel's time as a people.
The text does not specify whom the people address, so saying they tell each other adds a detail.
This is the final choice card in a passage that is not the last in its story group, but the explanation does not say the story is not over.
